assessment: The source provides a complete numerical study of spontaneous quantum turbulence in a 2D BEC via the Kibble-Zurek mechanism, with quantitative controls (quench time, temperature), readouts (vortex number, equilibration time, energy spectra, structure functions), and fitted power-law parameters. The evidence supports authoring an interactive experiment.

claims.applicability: Valid for 10 <= tau_Q <= 1000, at equilibration time, in the low-temperature limit.
claims.statement: The vortex number at equilibration time scales as n_v = (249.036 +/- 44.999) tau_Q^{-0.534 +/- 0.047}, consistent with the KZ prediction n_v ~ tau_Q^{-1/2}.
claims.statistical_basis: Averaged over R=1000 realizations; error bars 1 standard deviation.

claims.applicability: Valid for 10 <= tau_Q <= 1000, measured from critical crossing.
claims.statement: The equilibration time scales as t_eq = (3.779 +/- 0.693) tau_Q^{0.541 +/- 0.069} + (0.078 +/- 0.059) tau_Q, consistent with t_eq ~ tau_Q^{1/2}.
claims.statistical_basis: Averaged over R=1000 realizations; error bars 1 standard deviation.
claims.uncertainty: Exponent uncertainty 0.069, amplitude uncertainty 0.693, linear coefficient uncertainty 0.059.

claims.applicability: At equilibration time, for tau_Q=100, in the inertial range and high-k range.
claims.quantitative_form: E_i(k) = 176.555 * k^{-1.710} for inertial range; E_i(k) = 1028.257 * k^{-3.025} for high-k
claims.statement: For tau_Q=100, the incompressible energy spectrum follows E_i(k) = 176.555 k^{-1.710} in the inertial range and E_i(k) = 1028.257 k^{-3.025} at high k.
claims.statistical_basis: Averaged over R=1000 realizations; error bands 1 standard deviation.

claims.applicability: At equilibration time, for tau_Q=350, in the inertial range and high-k range.
claims.quantitative_form: E_i(k) = 37.722 * k^{-1.654} for inertial range; E_i(k) = 226.968 * k^{-3.036} for high-k
claims.statement: For tau_Q=350, the incompressible energy spectrum follows E_i(k) = 37.722 k^{-1.654} in the inertial range and E_i(k) = 226.968 k^{-3.036} at high k.
claims.statistical_basis: Averaged over R=1000 realizations; error bands 1 standard deviation.

anchors.support: Panel (b) shows <E_i(k)> tau_Q^{3/4} vs k tau_Q^{1/4}.

claims.applicability: For tau_Q values in the KZ regime (tau_Q > 10), at equilibration time.
claims.statement: The incompressible energy spectra for different tau_Q collapse onto a universal curve when plotted as E_i(k) tau_Q^{3/4} vs k tau_Q^{1/4}.
claims.statistical_basis: Averaged over R=1000 realizations; 95% confidence interval in panel (b).
claims.uncertainty: Shaded error bands indicate 95% confidence interval.

claims.statement: At T=1, the compressible energy is nearly independent of tau_Q, with E_c = (3.977 +/- 0.120) x 10^3 tau_Q^{-0.019 +/- 0.006}.
claims.statistical_basis: Averaged over R=1000 realizations; error bars 1 standard deviation.

claims.statement: At T=10^-6, the compressible energy scales as E_c = (7.422 +/- 4.679) x 10^3 tau_Q^{-0.902 +/- 0.131}, consistent with tau_Q^{-1}.
claims.statistical_basis: Averaged over R=2000 realizations; error bars 1 standard deviation.

anchors.support: Fitted relations for S_1, S_2, S_4, S_5.

claims.applicability: For tau_Q=350, at equilibration time, over r range 0.03 to 15.
claims.quantitative_form: S_p = A_p [S_3]^{zeta(p)} with zeta(p) = p/3 - 0.114 p (p-3)/2
claims.statement: For tau_Q=350, the structure functions satisfy S_1 = 0.420 [S_3]^{0.439}, S_2 = 0.457 [S_3]^{0.820}, S_4 = 3.316 [S_3]^{1.069}, S_5 = 13.794 [S_3]^{1.118}, with exponents described by K62 with kappa = 0.114.
claims.statistical_basis: Averaged over R=1000 realizations; error bars 1 standard deviation.
claims.uncertainty: Exponents and amplitudes as given; kappa uncertainty 0.006.

anchors.support: Linear quench mu(t) = mu_i + (mu_f - mu_i) t/tau_Q.

controls.definition: Duration of the linear quench of the chemical potential from mu_i to mu_f.
controls.name: quench_time

controls.definition: Temperature in dimensionless units, with T=1 corresponding to O(1) nK.
controls.name: temperature

fixed_conditions.statement: Simulation parameters: L=30, t_r=10, mu_i=0.1, mu_f=20, g=1, gamma=0.03, T=1, epsilon_cut=2.5 mu_f.
The system is a periodic L x L homogeneous box with V(r)=0 and initial condition Psi_C=0.

anchors.support: Low-temperature limit of order 1 nK or less.

fixed_conditions.statement: Work in the low-temperature limit (of order 1 nK or less) to isolate SQT from BKT effects.
Use mean-field critical exponents nu=1/2 and z=2.

anchors.support: KZM predicts vortex density scaling rho_v ~ tau_Q^{-2 nu/(1+z nu)} and freeze-out time scaling.
Vortex number scales as n_v ~ tau_Q^{-1/2}, with fit n_v = (249.036 +/- 44.999) tau_Q^{-0.534 +/- 0.047}.

mechanisms.statement: During a finite-time quench through the BEC transition, the Kibble-Zurek mechanism predicts the formation of vortices with density scaling as rho_v ~ tau_Q^{-2 nu/(1+z nu)} and freeze-out time scaling as tau_Q^{z nu/(1+z nu)}.

anchors.support: Kolmogorov scaling E_i(k) ~ k^{-5/3} in inertial range.
At higher momenta, E_i(k) ~ k^{-3} due to vortex core.
Fitted exponents and amplitudes for tau_Q=100 and 350.

E_i(k) = B k^{-beta} for high-k range

paper_scope: Numerical simulations of the 2D stochastic projected Gross-Pitaevskii equation for a homogeneous BEC quenched through the condensation transition, establishing Kibble-Zurek scaling of vortex number and equilibration time, Kolmogorov scaling of the incompressible kinetic energy spectrum, and universal collapse of spectra under KZ rescaling.

source.citation: Seong-Ho Shinn et al., Spontaneous Quantum Turbulence in a Newborn Bose-Einstein Condensate via the Kibble-Zurek Mechanism, Physical Review Letters (2026), DOI:10.1103/b16v-hwp2

anchors.support: Main text fit without linear term.

source_ambiguities.statement: The main text reports t_eq = (3.779 +/- 0.693) tau_Q^{0.541 +/- 0.069} without a linear term, while the supplementary material includes an additional linear term (0.078 +/- 0.059) tau_Q. The main text may have omitted the linear term for brevity.

anchors.support: Weighted least squares with weights given by inverse variances.

source_ambiguities.statement: The paper does not specify whether reported plus/minus values are standard errors, standard deviations, or confidence intervals. For fits, they are likely standard errors from weighted least squares, but this is not explicitly stated.
